claims.claim: Nextpower's structural path runs from electricity demand and renewable buildout through solar tracking, power conversion, storage and controls; Prevalon extends that path toward grid/power-quality constraints around AI data centers.

The broader platform can reduce dependence on tracker hardware, but successor bottlenecks move to storage/inverter integration, interconnection/project timing, trade-policy costs and proving that acquired technologies convert backlog into profitable deployed systems.

factors.name: crossDivisionLeverage
factors.basis: Tracking, eBOS, power conversion and storage can address multiple layers of utility-scale power deployment.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Electricity demand supports the platform while solar/project policy, tariffs and acquisition execution can change economics.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: System integration can add stickiness, but trackers, inverters and BESS remain competitive markets.

risks.risk: Platform breadth creates integration complexity and does not guarantee cross-selling or superior economics.

causalEdges.mechanism: new generation requires physical optimization, conversion, balancing and controls
causalEdges.falsifier: project economics/policy or competing architectures materially reduce deployment

causalEdges.mechanism: combined tracker/eBOS/inverter/storage capabilities can reduce system friction and address power quality
causalEdges.falsifier: integration fails or customers prefer best-of-breed alternatives without platform premium

unknowns.unknown: Long-run margins and cross-selling economics of the acquired storage/power-conversion platform are not yet established.

claims.claim: Prevalon closed in July 2026 and contributed backlog above $300M, resolving the earlier Scout unknown about closing status, but integration and economic-conversion risk remain.
Backlog above $5.5B is evidence of demand, not guaranteed revenue or margin; tariffs on steel, solar components and batteries can pressure project economics and customer timing.

factors.name: executionRisk
factors.basis: Transaction close is complete, but integration and conversion of acquired backlog remain future execution tasks.

factors.name: tradePolicyRisk
factors.basis: Steel and component tariffs can increase costs and reduce project viability.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: Large backlog should not be treated as equivalent to realized profitable revenue.

risks.risk: Acquisition integration and capital allocation can dilute platform benefits.
Tariffs and policy shifts can compress margins or delay customer projects.
Backlog can overstate near-term economic realization if schedules slip or project economics weaken.

causalEdges.mechanism: orders and acquired capabilities must convert through delivery, integration and margin realization
causalEdges.falsifier: sustained conversion, margins and customer retention demonstrate economic execution

contradictions.claim: Scout listed Prevalon closing status as unknown; later Q1 FY2027 filing states it closed in July 2026.
contradictions.resolution: Resolved by newer primary SEC-filed evidence; integration performance remains non-gating unknown.

unknowns.unknown: Post-close Prevalon margin, retention and return on invested capital are not yet established.
